transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net technical support, my name is Jessica. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Jessica. I am at my absolute wits' end with this broadband. Every single time it rains, our internet drops out every ten minutes, and I got disconnected from an executive board meeting twice this morning! It is completely intolerable!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Can I take your full installation postcode and your four-digit security PIN to open your broadband file?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's 54 Highfield Avenue, Sheffield, S11 9EL, and the PIN is 3820.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you. What color is the broadband light on your router when the drops occur?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It flashes orange and then takes about three minutes to go solid white again.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am running our automated cabinet copper test on the line now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does the test show the line dropping?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So if I have understood correctly, your VDSL service functions normally during dry weather, but during rainfall, the connection suffers frequent sync drops and takes several minutes to retrain. Is that right, Isabella?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly. It has been happening for three weeks now. The moment the clouds open up, the broadband becomes completely unstable.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That symptom strongly indicates water ingress inside the street underground distribution joint or the pole DP casing.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Water getting into the cables outside?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes. When rain enters an unsealed joint box in the pavement, it creates a resistive ground fault between the copper leg wires, causing high loop attenuation.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you see that on your line diagnostics?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, our copper test shows a battery contact resistance imbalance of 180 ohms on Leg B during damp conditions.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is that something you can fix remotely or does an Openreach engineer have to come out?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Because the physical fault is located in the street cabling, it requires an external infrastructure engineer to locate and reseal the joint.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Do I have to wait at home all day for an engineer if the fault is outside in the road?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No, Isabella. This is classified as an External Network Repair. The engineer will carry out all work at the street cabinet and underground footway box.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is such a relief, I don't have to take a half day off work.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Where is your router located inside the house? Is it plugged into the master socket or an extension?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's plugged directly into the master socket in the hallway with the original gray cable.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And have you tried replacing the DSL microfilter between the wall and the Hub?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I swapped the microfilter on Tuesday with a spare one from the box, but it made no difference when it rained.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That further confirms the fault is external on the physical copper pair rather than internal household wiring.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will the engineer test the line from the street cabinet down to our house?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, the technician will use a Time Domain Reflectometer at the street cabinet to trace the exact meterage of the high resistance fault.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How long does an external repair like that normally take?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Once the engineer accesses the footway box, splicing a new waterproof gel crimp connector typically takes between one and two hours.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What happens if it starts raining heavily while the engineer is working in the street box?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Openreach engineers erect all-weather canopy tents over the pavement footway chamber and use moisture-barrier gel sleeves, so the repair is fully protected.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And when will the engineer be assigned to the job?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have an engineer slot available tomorrow morning between eight and one o'clock.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Tomorrow morning would be fantastic. My mobile number is zero seven eight nine one, four four three two one zero for the engineer updates.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is zero seven eight nine one, four four three two one zero the best mobile contact number for SMS appointment tracking?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that is my direct work mobile.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have registered that number for automated SMS notifications when the engineer arrives on site and completes the repair.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will our internet go down while the engineer works on the street box?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, expect a brief disconnection of approximately twenty minutes while the pair is crimped and resealed in the joint.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's completely fine since you told me in advance.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please bear with me while I place you on a brief hold for about two minutes while I book the external engineering ticket on the Openreach portal.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for your patience while holding, Isabella. The Openreach external fault ticket has been logged under reference OR-992817.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Got that reference written down, thank you.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: After the physical repair completes tomorrow, our Dynamic Line Management system will monitor your line for 48 hours to restore maximum sync speed.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does DLM slow down the line automatically when errors happen?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes. Because of the frequent dropouts, DLM increased your signal-to-noise margin to twelve decibels to prevent total loss of sync.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So once the water leak is fixed, the line will speed back up?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Once the copper pair is clean and dry, DLM will lower the target margin back to six decibels, restoring your full seventy-six megabit download speed.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That explains why speeds felt slower even between drops.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Are we eligible for automatic compensation for the loss of service while this was happening?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Under Ofcom's automatic compensation code of practice, if a broadband fault is not rectified within two full working days of reporting, an automatic credit of £9.76 per calendar day applies.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does that show up automatically on our monthly bill or do we have to submit a claim?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The credit applies automatically to your billing ledger without requiring any manual paperwork.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does the compensation continue adding up daily until the line stabilizes?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, the daily credit accrues automatically until the physical repair is certified by the Openreach network operations center.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is very reassuring to know.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How will I know when the engineer has completed the splicing work in the street tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The technician conducts a metallic loop line test directly to the master socket, which triggers an automated SMS notification saying external fault cleared.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And do I need to restart our Hub router once the text message arrives?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, power-cycling the Hub once the repair is complete clears any old error counters in the modem chipset and starts clean synchronization.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'll make sure to power-cycle it as soon as the text comes through.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Will you require a temporary four-G mobile data backup dongle while the repair is pending?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, tomorrow morning is very quick so my phone hotspot will cover the evening.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If the rain starts again tonight and the line drops, leaving the router powered on allows DLM to keep accurate error logs.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I won't turn the router off, I'll leave it plugged in.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And you will receive a final confirmation text message once the engineer runs the post-repair copper pass test.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That gives me great peace of mind.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else regarding your broadband service that I can check for you today, Isabella?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, Jessica, you've diagnosed the issue and booked the engineer very quickly. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net today, Isabella. Have a wonderful rest of your day.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks Jessica, goodbye.
